name: Billabong Sanctuary
note: Wildlife park: a visitor attraction 20 minutes from the city with koalas, crocodiles, bilbies and feeding shows.

name: Museum of Underwater Art
note: Underwater sculpture museum on John Brewer Reef, reached by diving: the Coral Greenhouse and installations.

name: Perc Tucker Regional Gallery
note: Art gallery: a regional gallery with over 2,000 artworks and touring exhibitions in Townsville.

name: Maritime Museum of Townsville
note: Museum: recovered shipwreck artefacts, model ships and North Queensland wartime history.

name: Cape Pallarenda
note: Bushland headland north of the city: mountain bike trails, WWII fortifications and a historic quarantine station.

name: Anderson Gardens
note: Botanic garden: one of Townsville's three botanic gardens, with a conservatory.

name: Queensland Country Bank Stadium
note: Stadium: home ground of the NRL Cowboys and a concert venue; an event venue, judge against the bar.

name: Cotters Market
note: Weekly market: runs only on Sundays in Flinders Street, so it is not a permanent spot; listed for judging.

name: Tan Lines Distilling
note: Distillery: tasting sessions at a saltwater pool on The Strand; a venue, judge against the bar.

name: Ardo Rooftop
note: Hotel bar: rooftop bar at the Ardo hotel on the coast; a venue, not a visitor attraction on its own.

name: The Strand Water Park
note: Free water playground on The Strand, part of the Strand promenade.

name: Hervey's Range Heritage Tea Rooms
note: Tea rooms: heritage building begun in 1865 as the Eureka Hotel, atop Hervey's Range west of Townsville.

name: Gilberton Outback Retreat
note: Accommodation: a private cattle station retreat, 6 hours from Townsville; accommodation, not a spot.

name: Hidden Valley Platypus Safari
note: Wildlife tour: two-hour guided platypus viewing in Hidden Valley, about two hours north of Townsville.

name: Towers Hill
note: Lookout and heritage hill: WWII bunkers, a 2.5 km walk, rock wallabies and views over Charters Towers.

name: Stock Exchange Arcade
note: Heritage building: the Mosman Street arcade that was the Charters Towers Stock Exchange from 1890 to 1916.

name: Ghosts of Gold Heritage Trail
note: Heritage trail: a self-guided walk and audio drive of 30 gold-rush sites in Charters Towers.

name: Miners' Memorial Walk
note: Memorial walk: honours those killed in mine, mill and quarry accidents in Charters Towers.

name: Historic Ambulance Museum
note: Museum: a 1903 ambulance station, the first outside Brisbane, in Charters Towers.

name: Pioneer Cemetery
note: Cemetery: graves of 1872 to 1895 gold-rush pioneers in Charters Towers; a historical stop.

name: Dalrymple Saleyards
note: Cattle saleyards: livestock sales most Wednesdays; a working operation, judge against the bar.

name: Centenary Park
note: Park: a gold discovery monument and sculptures by Queensland artist Hugh Anderson in Charters Towers.

name: Ravenswood
note: Heritage township: a gold-mining town 89 km east of Charters Towers, with a courthouse museum and silhouette sculptures.

name: Young's Block Fossicking
note: Fossicking area: gold collecting locality 15 km from Charters Towers.

name: Ingham
note: Town: hub of the Hinchinbrook region with a strong Italian food scene (delis, pasta, bakeries) and the Hinchinbrook Visitor Information Centre.

name: Mercer Lane Street Art
note: Street art: laneway murals in Ingham, named as a stop alongside the town's galleries.

name: Wallaman Falls
note: Waterfall: Australia's highest single-drop waterfall at 268 m, in Girringun National Park west of Ingham.

name: Girringun National Park
note: National park: World Heritage rainforest and falls around Wallaman Falls and Mount Fox.

name: Jourama Falls
note: Waterfall and swimming holes: a 3 km return walk through woodland and rainforest in Paluma Range area.

name: Paluma Range National Park
note: National park: rainforest waterfalls, Mount Spec and camping and swimming near Paluma Village.

name: Mount Spec
note: Mountain: rises nearly 1,000 m above the plains in Paluma Range National Park; access by permit only at present.

name: Lake Paluma
note: Lake: a camping and swimming spot at Paluma in the Paluma Range.

name: Mount Fox
note: Volcanic crater: an extinct volcano in Girringun National Park with walking tracks and a lookout over the Herbert Valley.

name: Trebonne
note: Rural village: a gateway to Wallaman Falls and Broadwater State Forest, 10 km north-west of Ingham.

name: Broadwater State Forest
note: State forest: a forest and falls area reached from Trebonne, part of the Hinchinbrook Way.

name: Halifax
note: Historic village: a heritage township on the Herbert River with local history to share.

name: Forrest Beach
note: Coastal village: a long open beach for walks, swimming and watching the waves.

name: Taylors Beach
note: Coastal village: fishing and boating base, with soldier crabs on the mudflats at low tide.

name: Dungeness
note: Coastal village: departure point for Zoe Bay trips to Hinchinbrook Island, with fishing and walking trails.

name: Lucinda
note: Coastal village: long beachfront and the ferry gateway to Orpheus and Hinchinbrook islands; a gateway, judge against the bar.

name: Hinchinbrook Island
note: Island national park: Australia's largest island national park, largely uninhabited, reached by boat.

name: Thorsborne Trail
note: Multi-day hike: a moderately demanding track along the east coast of Hinchinbrook Island, booked well ahead.

name: Zoe Falls
note: Waterfall: natural infinity pools at the base of Zoe Falls, about 900 m inland from South Zoe Bay on Hinchinbrook Island.

name: Zoe Bay
note: Beach: the main visitor landing on Hinchinbrook Island, the start for Zoe Falls.

name: Orpheus Island
note: Island: a resort island on the Great Barrier Reef for snorkelling, diving and sunsets, reached from Lucinda.

name: Pelorus Island
note: Island: a secluded reef island 800 m north of Orpheus Island, with snorkelling and diving.

name: SS Yongala
note: Shipwreck dive: a wreck off Ayr ranked among the world's best wreck dives, teeming with marine life.

name: Geoffrey Bay
note: Bay: self-guided snorkelling trail off the beach on Magnetic Island.

name: Ayr
note: Town: Burdekin sister town to Home Hill and the base for SS Yongala dives.

name: Home Hill
note: Town: a Burdekin sister town across the Burdekin River bridge, with cafes and local produce.
